subject: Transient surge quota crediting framework and cooldown — proposal

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Draft surge credits + cooldown approach for Dedicated pool

Hi Ashok / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attaching a short draft of the Dedicated pricing worksheet that shows how transient surge capacity (what we called "ephemeral spikes") would be handled on top of Finnotech's reserved commit. Key things I pulled together for clarity:

- A short surge credit pool (monthly) that can be consumed at a 3x per-minute token throughput multiplier for short windows.
- A cooldown period (windowed) after sustained usage above the reserved throughput where charges revert to a higher surge rate.
- A soft cap (automated throttling) to prevent runaway spend if multiple containers scale simultaneously.

I've attached "Finnotech-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf" with the worked examples. Please review and let me know which of the three consumption profiles (pilot, steady-state, rapid-burst) maps best to your Q3/production needs.

Action: if you can confirm which profile you expect (pilot vs steady-state vs rapid-burst) by end of next week, we’ll finalize the SOW and send a DocuSign link.

Cheers,
Ben

Subject: Re: Draft surge credits + cooldown approach for Dedicated pool

Ben —

Thanks for the summary and file. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop in finance:

1) How do you measure the start of the cooldown period? Is it per-GPU pool, per-customer, or per-model? We have differing workloads routed to the same pool and want to avoid one noisy job triggering cooldown for all traffic.
2) In the worked example the surge rate jumps 4x after cooldown. Can that be smoothed (e.g., graduated steps) instead of a single cliff?
3) For the short-term pilot, can you cap monthly surge spend so we don’t exceed a fixed overage budget?

Also looping in Vikram from Ops in case he has infra constraints.

—Ashok
Ashok Mehta
Head of ML Platforms | Finnotech

Subject: Re: Draft surge credits + cooldown approach for Dedicated pool

Hi Ashok — great questions. Quick answers and a concrete proposal below. I’ve also added Marissa (pricing) and Karthik (Dedicated product) to make sure we capture operational constraints.

1) Cooldown semantics: per-customer-per-pool with model-aware tagging. Practically that means we track sustained throughput above the reserved commit aggregated at the pool level, but we can scope cooldowns using a label for high-noise jobs so they don't penalize unrelated routes. If you want strict isolation, we can create a small dedicated shard for the noisy model (cost tradeoff).

2) Graduated surge tiers: yes — we can replace the single-step cliff with a 3-band graduated surcharge:
   - Tier A (short spikes): up to 15 minutes at 3x baseline throughput, billed at +40% unit rate, consumed from the monthly surge credit pool.
   - Tier B (prolonged spike): 15–60 minutes at 2x baseline throughput, billed at +75% unit rate, subject to a 2-hour cooldown window.
   - Tier C (sustained overload): >60 minutes at >1.5x baseline, billed at +200% unit rate and requires operational review — auto-throttle protects core traffic.

3) Monthly overage cap for pilots: we can set a hard cap and suspend surge consumption when hit — with an optional manual-override button for emergency bursts. Suggestion: start pilot with a $15k monthly surge cap and evaluate.

Concrete ask: Please confirm which isolation model you prefer (label-based cooldown or dedicated shard) and whether the $15k pilot cap is acceptable. Once we have that, Marissa will provide a final pricing addendum and a SOW update.

Attachment: SOW-Finnotech-Redwood-v2.docx (contains the draft language for the cap and graduated tiers).

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Ashok / Vikram —

Thanks for the quick feedback and Camila for the detailed proposal. From a sales/contracting side we can accommodate the graduated tiers + $15k cap for the pilot. A couple of contract notes:

- We’ll include a line item for the pilot cap and a clause for manual override with both parties' written sign-off.
- If Finnotech wants label-based scoping instead of a dedicated shard, we’ll confirm model tagging requirements in the SOW and target a 2–3 week operational onboarding window.

Next step: once Ashok confirms isolation preference (label-based or dedicated shard) we’ll circulate the final SOW and DocuSign link.
